anchor: nothing especially german to the story
note: Germane: relevant, closely connected to the subject.

anchor: line-of-battle ships
note: Line-of-battle ships were the largest warships, built to fight in a line against enemy fleets.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Line-of-battle ship”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: the English squadron up the Straits
note: The Straits are the Strait of Gibraltar, the narrow gateway from the Atlantic into the Mediterranean Sea.

anchor: not common in a ship of her rate
note: A ship’s rate was her class, set by her number of guns.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Rate”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: a prompt initiative might have to be taken
note: Initiative: the power or readiness to act first.

anchor: in the latter part of an afternoon-watch
note: The afternoon watch lasted from noon to four.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Afternoon-watch”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: invoking her light heels
note: The enemy frigate trusts to her speed to escape.

anchor: crowded sail to get away
note: To crowd sail is to spread as many sails as possible.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Crowd”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: ere the excitement incident thereto
note: Incident thereto: connected with it.

anchor: ascending from his cavernous sphere
note: Cavernous: like a cave. The lower decks are Claggart’s domain.

anchor: cap in hand by the main-mast
note: A lower-rank man waited by the mainmast to ask the captain for a hearing.

anchor: somewhat chafed at the failure of the pursuit
note: Chafed: irritated, annoyed by the failed chase.

anchor: the officer-of-the-deck
note: The officer of the deck is the officer in charge of the ship during a watch.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Officer of the watch”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: the doffed cap held in deferential expectancy
note: Doffed: taken off as a sign of respect.

anchor: a vaguely repellent distaste
note: Repellent: causing dislike or disgust.

anchor: resuming much of his wonted official manner
note: Wonted: usual, accustomed, as in his wonted manner.

anchor: to disburthen, spoke up
note: Disburthen: to unload, here to speak out freely.

anchor: Be direct, man; say impressed men.
note: Impressed men were those forced into the navy. Vere dislikes polite evasions about them, and says so.

anchor: Claggart made a gesture of subservience
note: Subservience: humble, servile obedience to a superior.

anchor: the first broaching of the matter
note: Broaching: bringing up a subject for the first time.

anchor: could not wholly dissemble his disquietude
note: Dissemble: to hide one’s true feelings. Disquietude: worry, unease.

anchor: restiveness under something in the witness’ manner
note: Restiveness: restlessness, resistance to control.

anchor: peremptorily broke in
note: Peremptorily: in a commanding way that allows no argument.

anchor: the Nore Mutiny had assumed a singularly tragical character
note: At the Nore in 1797 the mutinous crews took over their ships. Claggart nearly names a ship whose commander’s life was in danger.

anchor: a most immodest presumption
note: Presumption: overstepping one’s place and showing too much boldness.

anchor: an intuitional surmise
note: Intuitional: arising from instinct, not reasoning.

anchor: its secret mines and dubious side
note: Dubious: doubtful, not to be trusted.

anchor: the first palpable sign of recurring insubordination
note: Palpable: so clear it can almost be touched. Insubordination: refusal to obey.

anchor: police surveillance of the crew
note: Surveillance: close watching of people.

anchor: rather supersensible and strained
note: Supersensible: too sensitive, overly alert to danger.

anchor: a bandsman, a perjurous witness
note: Perjurous: lying under oath. Vere recalls a false witness he had once seen at a court-martial.

anchor: a capital case before a courtmartial
note: A capital case is one where the penalty may be death. A court-martial is a military trial.

anchor: with unfeigned astonishment
note: Unfeigned: real, not pretended or put on for effect.

anchor: a deep one
note: A deep one: a person who hides his thoughts and intentions.

anchor: insinuate himself into the good will of his shipmates
note: Insinuate: to work oneself gradually into favor by clever means.

anchor: that adroit fling of Budd’s
note: Adroit: skillful, clever. Fling: here, a jibe.

anchor: masqued by that sort of good-humoured air
note: Masqued: masked, hidden. His good humor hides resentment, Claggart says.

anchor: A man-trap may be under his ruddy-tipped daisies
note: A man-trap is a snare for people. Claggart pictures a trap hidden under a flowery bank.

anchor: the genus homo, who in the nude might have posed for a statue of young Adam before the Fall
note: Homo is the Latin genus of humans. Adam before the Fall was the first man, sinless, in Eden.
source: The Bible (King James Version), Genesis 2:25, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10

anchor: a satiric sally
note: Sally: a sudden witty remark.

anchor: the first happy augury
note: Augury: a sign or omen of future events.

anchor: the captaincy of the mizzentop
note: The captain of a top commanded the men working there. The mizzentop is on the mizzenmast, the rear mast.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Mizzen-top”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: the starboard watch
note: Sailors were divided into two watches, port and starboard, that took turns on duty.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Watch”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: striplings
note: Striplings: youths just growing up.

anchor: a “King’s bargain,”
note: A King’s bargain was a navy phrase for a man gotten for nothing, a bargain for the Crown.

anchor: a capital investment at small outlay or none at all
note: Capital: excellent. Outlay: money spent.

anchor: there is a yard-arm-end for the false-witness
note: Vere threatens to hang a false witness from the yard-arm.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Yard-arm”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: sad deprecation of such unmerited severity
note: Deprecation: mild disapproval, here an injured, sorrowful shake of the head.

anchor: he circumstantially alleged certain words and acts
note: Circumstantially: with detailed circumstances, giving many particular facts.

anchor: presumptions mortally inculpating Budd
note: Inculpating: showing to be guilty.

anchor: averments
note: Averments: formal statements asserting that something is true.

anchor: the spokesman of the envious children of Jacob
note: Jacob’s sons, jealous of their brother Joseph, dipped his coat in goat’s blood and showed it to their father as proof he was dead.
source: The Bible (King James Version), Genesis 37:31, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10

anchor: a veritable touch-stone of that man’s essential nature
note: A touchstone is a stone used to test gold’s purity; Vere tests men’s character likewise.

anchor: strong suspicion clogged by strange dubieties
note: Dubieties: doubts, uncertainties that cloud his judgment.

anchor: before trying the accusation, he would first practically test the accuser
note: Vere decides to examine the witness before the accused.

anchor: the few gun-room officers
note: The gun-room was the mess of the junior officers, on the lower deck.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Gun-room”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: in due observance of naval etiquette
note: Etiquette: the rules of polite behavior.

anchor: the colloquy with Claggart
note: Colloquy: a formal conversation between two people.

anchor: the waist
note: The waist is the middle part of the ship’s upper deck.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Waist”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: summoning the nearest midshipman
note: A midshipman was a young officer in training.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Midshipman”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: the Captain’s hammock-boy, a sort of sea-valet
note: Valet: a man who looks after another’s clothes and needs.

anchor: Contrive it that he speaks to nobody
note: Contrive: to arrange cleverly, here to manage it without being noticed.
